backfill_note: The experiments were run firsthand on 2026-06-21 (same day as the post) on a Windows machine, and the observations recorded in the post are taken from that session. The exact ad-hoc shell commands were not retained; this run directory reconstructs a runnable harness (the .tf fixtures + run.sh) from the fully-documented experiment steps. The fixtures reproduce the documented behavior — they are not a fresh 2026-08 re-measurement.

environment.note: This is a CLI plan/destroy-semantics check across two OpenTofu versions, not a timing benchmark. CPU/GPU/RAM do not affect the result, so they are intentionally omitted. The provider under test is hashicorp/local, so no cloud credentials or remote objects are involved.

subject.name: opentofu
subject.note: 1.12.0 released 2026-05-14; re-verified on 1.12.3 (latest patch, 2026-06-18). Behavior identical across 1.12.0 -> 1.12.3.

baseline.name: opentofu
baseline.note: Prior minor, used as contrast for Exp A (variable-driven prevent_destroy). No timing comparison; the contrast is validate-time accept/reject behavior.

cross_tool.terraform: NOT measured locally — no terraform binary installed. The Exp R claim that Terraform defaults to *destroy* (vs OpenTofu's *forget*) when the removed block omits lifecycle is cited from HashiCorp docs, explicitly flagged as not-firsthand.

source_of_truth: CHANGELOG.md shipped inside the 1.12.0 release zip (cross-checked against observed CLI behavior).

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: none discarded — all evidence for this run is small and committed
raw_artifacts.note: This run produces no large raw artifacts. The deterministic evidence is the CLI plan verbs and exit codes captured in results.json; the .tf fixtures and run.sh regenerate them. terraform.tfstate is transient and intentionally not committed (it embeds absolute local paths and is regenerable by run.sh).
